data.one_liner: A static wrapper around shared_preferences for reading and writing app preferences.
data.what_it_does: It wraps the shared_preferences plugin to store and read key-value preferences across Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux. It provides a static class interface to easily get and set values without needing an instance.
use_when: You want a simpler static interface over shared_preferences
You need to store simple key-value data on the device
avoid_when: You need secure storage for sensitive data like passwords or tokens
You are looking for a robust type-safe ORM or NoSQL database
strengths: Static function calls make it accessible anywhere in the app
Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux
weaknesses: Relies on shared_preferences which does not guarantee writes to disk
Not suitable for critical data storage
data.setup_notes: Initialize the class library using Prefs.init() or Prefs.initAsync() in your app's initState() and clean up with Prefs.dispose() in dispose().

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: You prefer using the official low-level plugin directly without a third-party static wrapper.

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: You need secure encrypted storage instead of plain key-value preferences.
